source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
After reviewing the schematic and PCB files closely, I think the board looks solid overall and the work is good. Could you examine these observations and share your thoughts?

1\. For the USB-C connector (USB1), DRC reports hole-clearance violations and negative annular width on the 2 mounting pin holes. The drills appear larger than their copper pads. Will JLCPCB accept the footprint as it is, or must it be fixed?
2. On the PCB, VMID (pin 36) of AXP2101 shares a net with VSYS. Because VMID should be the internal ADC reference, I would expect only a capacitor to GND and isolation from VSYS. Could you verify this against the datasheet or a reference design?
3. Although D1 is marked DNP, its current-limiting resistor R6 (4.7k) remains in the BOM and would be assembled. With D1 unplaced, one R6 pin would float. Is there a reason to retain R6, or should R6 also be DNP?
4. To avoid confusion, the VSIS net name is worth correcting because it appears to be a typo for VSYS.
5\. For L1, DRC says the Inductor_SMD:L_Changjiang_FTC404020S footprint is absent from the standard KiCad library and uses a local override. Please confirm that its physical dimensions match the intended 4.7uH inductor.

value_updates.vmid_vsys_reference_conformance: The VMID and VSYS topology must be verified against the AXP2101 datasheet or an applicable reference design.

source_message.text: I did misread this, sorry. Because the AXP is complicated and will be used in many places, I was overly cautious about it. Any power-related error would be impossible to repair later given the chip's 0.9mm size.

routing_warnings.description: The DCDC1 3.4V setpoint clause concerns the separate power-board output-setpoint Requirement rather than core AXP2101 topology.
The decision to retain AXP2101 concerns the later integrated-board power-management architecture.
The request to expose PWROK and VBACKUP belongs to the integrated-board auxiliary-pin Requirement.
The contiguous pours and stitching-via requirements concern integrated-board high-current routing.
The manufactured-board L3 voltage instability concerns integrated-board DCDC1 regulation and load stability, not the earlier power-board topology Requirement.
The unsuccessful AXP2101 replacement concerns integrated-board assembly reliability.
